title: उपमानप्रमाणविवेचनम्
nepali: प्राच्यदर्शनेषु प्रमाणनिरूपणं सर्वैरपि यथामतं विधीयते । प्रमाणविवेचनपूर्वकमेवदर्शनशास्त्रस्यावबोधो भवति । एवंञ्च प्रमाणविभागोऽपि दर्शनदृष्ट्यनुसारेण विहितो दृश्यते ।प्रमाणसंख्यायामपि नास्त्यैकत्वमिति । बौद्धाःतत्र प्रत्यक्षानुमानमेव स्वीकुर्वन्ति । वैशेषिकाऽपिप्रमाणद्वयमेव स्वीकुर्वन्ति । एवं क्रमेण प्रमाणसंख्यायामपि भेदोऽपलभ्यते । न्यायमतेप्रत्यक्षानुमानोपमानशब्दा इति चत्वरि प्रमाणानि स्वीक्रियन्ते । तत्रोपमानप्रमाणं मीमांसावेदान्तादिष्वपिगृह्यते । उपमानप्रमाणनिरूपणञ्च न्यायदर्शनादन्यथा एव मीमांसादिषु विहितं वर्तते । तस्यउपमानस्य विषये अत्र संक्षिप्तमात्रेण अत्र मया प्रदर्शितमस्ति ।
american_english: In Eastern philosophies, the determination of epistemic means (pramana) is carried out by all according to their respective doctrines. An understanding of philosophy arises only following a critical examination of pramana. And likewise, the division of pramanas is also observed to be laid down in accordance with the philosophical viewpoint. Nor is there unanimity regarding the number of pramanas. Therein, the Buddhists accept only perception (pratyaksha) and inference (anumana). The Vaisheshikas as well accept only these two pramanas. In this manner, divergence is encountered concerning the number of pramanas. In the Nyaya view, four pramanas are accepted, namely perception, inference, comparison (upamana), and verbal testimony (shabda). Among them, the pramana of comparison is also accepted in Mimamsa, Vedanta, and other systems. Furthermore, the elucidation of upamana pramana in Mimamsa and other schools is formulated quite differently from that in the Nyaya philosophy. Concerning that very upamana, I have presented an exposition here in a concise manner.

informal_english: In Eastern philosophies, you see, the determination of epistemic means (pramana) is carried out by all according to their respective doctrines. An understanding of philosophy arises only following a critical examination of pramana, fair play. And sure enough, the division of pramanas is also observed to be laid down in accordance with the philosophical viewpoint. Nor is there any unanimity regarding the number of pramanas, at all. Therein, the Buddhists accept only perception (pratyaksha) and inference (anumana). The Vaisheshikas as well accept only these two pramanas, nothing more. In this manner, divergence is clearly encountered concerning the number of pramanas. In the Nyaya view, four pramanas are accepted, namely perception, inference, comparison (upamana), and verbal testimony (shabda). Among them, the pramana of comparison is also accepted in Mimamsa, Vedanta, and other systems, grand as you like. Furthermore, the elucidation of upamana pramana in Mimamsa and other schools is formulated quite differently from that in the Nyaya philosophy. Concerning that very upamana, I have presented an exposition here in a good and concise manner.
translator_notes: Source abstract is written in classical Sanskrit prose. Epistemological technical terms transliterated and rendered: pramana (means of knowledge), pratyaksha (perception), anumana (inference), upamana (comparison), shabda (verbal testimony). Strict 11-sentence order maintained.
